title: Restriction of scalars identifies strict Koszul towers and their units
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\varphi:R\to B$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ a finite list of global sections of $R$, allowing $r=0$. Assume $B$ is flat over $R$, meaning that $B\otimes_R-$ is exact. Use module sheaves and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For $O=R,B$, write $a_{j,R}=a_j$ and $a_{j,B}=\varphi(a_j)$, and define
$$Q_m(O)=\bigotimes_{j=1}^r[O\xrightarrow{a_{j,O}^m}O]\qquad(m\geq1)$$
in degrees $[-r,0]$, using the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Give these the inverse transition $(a_{j,O},1)$ in each two-term factor and the degree-zero maps $O[0]\to Q_m(O)$, as in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system]. For any unbounded $B$-module complex $C$, put $T_B(C)_m=\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_BQ_m(B))$ and $T_R(\operatorname{Res}C)_m=\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Res}C\otimes_RQ_m(R))$.

There is a canonical natural isomorphism of strict towers of complexes
$$\operatorname{Res}T_B(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_R(\operatorname{Res}C).$$
On the summand indexed by any exterior basis element it is the identity on $\operatorname{Res}C$. It commutes with the transition maps and the degree-zero maps from $\operatorname{Res}C$. With $R\lim$ the total right derived inverse limit of strict towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], this induces a natural isomorphism
$$\gamma_C:\operatorname{Res}(R\lim_m T_B(C)_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim_mT_R(\operatorname{Res}C)_m.$$
Writing $\eta_B$ and $\eta_R$ for the units induced by those degree-zero maps, one has $\gamma_C\circ\operatorname{Res}(\eta_B)=\eta_R$. The isomorphism also identifies every derived-limit evaluation with the corresponding restricted evaluation. These comparisons descend to $D(B)$ independently of the representative $C$. For $r=0$ they give the identity under the constant-tower identifications.

source.place: Tag 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul), finite free Koszul model; derived-limit restriction is Tag 0A07 (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), specialized to the identity topos with flat structural ring map. The strict tower, evaluation and unit normalization are made explicit.

proof.text: 1. Apply the strict scalar Koszul comparison to obtain the coordinate-normalized strict natural isomorphism h and its coaugmentation equation.

2. Obtain the presentations DB and DR, with the normalized Cech-completion comparison, directly from the proved single-site Cech/Koszul comparison. Descend h through localization, conjugating by the recorded tensor and exact-restriction factorizations; this gives hD with the displayed normalization.

3. Flat extension of scalars is an additive exact left adjoint to restriction. Whisker its adjunction by the tower shape; exactness remains pointwise. The right-adjoint criterion gives preservation of K-injective tower complexes. Restriction preserves ordinary limits. Apply the generic normalized limit-comparison construction from the pushforward comparison to DB and DR. Its normalization, after cancelling the exact-restriction factor, is the displayed equation for alpha. Obtain each p by the right-derived universal property applied to the ordinary limit projection.

4. Define gamma to be alpha on the derived tensor tower followed by derived inverse limit of hD. The strict coaugmentation is natural in complexes. Lift its ordinary-limit map to a natural transformation Id→completion and check that it equals the specified representative formula for D.unit. The strict coaugmentation equation, the normalization of hD and alpha, and naturality of the comparisons give the unit equation on complexes. Full faithfulness of localization transports it to all derived objects.

5. Apply right-derived uniqueness to compare alpha followed by the R-projection and evaluation comparison with the restricted B-projection. On complexes the equality is exactly the ordinary-limit projection identity, the projection normalizations and the factorization of the exact evaluation comparison. Naturality with hD then gives the displayed gamma projection square. This uses right-derived uniqueness, not detection of derived arrows by projections.

6. For r=0, use the normalized Cech-completion comparison supplied with the presentation. The empty Cech complex is the ring sheaf in degree zero with identity augmentation, whose completion unit is the evaluation-at-one derived Hom-unit isomorphism. Therefore D.unit is an isomorphism. Its inverse gives eB and eR. Cancel the invertible restricted B-unit in the already proved unit equation to obtain the final identity for gamma.
